channels.name: Ship landing page
channels.description: Design, build, and ship a high-converting Astro landing page.
channels.spec:
Goal: Ship one marketing page — hero, proof, features, FAQ, and a single CTA above the fold. Not an app, a dashboard, or a store.

## Stack
Astro with static output (`output: 'static'`), TypeScript, Tailwind, pnpm, ESM (`"type": "module"`). No Next.js, Remix, Nuxt, or a React SPA. No auth, billing, dashboard, catalog, or cart — those belong in Ship paid MVP or Ship ecommerce.

## Page
One primary CTA above the fold (waitlist, signup interest, or buy — whatever the brief says). Sections: hero, social proof, feature grid, FAQ. Real copy from the brief — no lorem ipsum, no placeholder company names once the product is known. Semantic HTML, mobile-first, accessible (labels, contrast, keyboard). Meta title, description, Open Graph, favicon. Keep JS minimal (Astro islands only if a form or accordion needs it). Waitlist or email capture is a client form with a success state. No database, no auth.

## Production
Push to GitHub and deploy as static hosting (prefer Cloudflare Pages). No VPS, Docker, or self-hosting.

## Agents
Claude Code builds the page and deploy config. GitHub hosts the repository. Firecrawl scrapes a reference URL when the human provides one (messaging, branding, visuals); rebuild a distinct page, do not copy it.

## Done when
The public preview matches the brief on mobile and desktop.

channels.name: Ship paid MVP
channels.description: Ship a paid MVP: Vite + React frontend, Express API, auth, payments, and email.
channels.spec:
Goal: Ship a paid MVP — one persona signs up, pays, and gets one confirmation email. Paywalled software, not a store or a marketing page.

## Stack
Two processes, not a fullstack monolith. pnpm, ESM.

- **Frontend:** Vite + React + TypeScript. React Router. Tailwind is fine. Call the API with relative `/api` URLs. Port 5173.
- **Backend:** a thin Express (or Hono) TypeScript server. JSON REST. Port 3001. Stripe webhooks, Resend, and any secret-bearing work live only here.
- **Do not** use Next.js, Remix, Nest, Redwood, or other fullstack frameworks. No React Server Components, no server actions.
- Layout: `frontend/`, `backend/`, root `package.json` scripts, and `.env.example`.
- Vite `server.proxy`: `/api` → `http://127.0.0.1:3001` so the browser uses one origin.

## Product slice
Match the brief's billing shape: subscription, one-time unlock, or usage-billed. A catalog, cart, or storefront belongs in Ship ecommerce. A marketing-only page belongs in Ship landing page.

- **Auth + data:** Supabase Auth and Postgres (Storage only if the slice needs it). Verify JWTs on the server. The service role key stays on the backend.
- **Payments:** Stripe Checkout. Create sessions on the server. Fulfill in the webhook (`checkout.session.completed` or invoice events) and make that handler idempotent. Never put the Stripe secret in the frontend.
- **Email:** Resend sends the success email (welcome, receipt, or magic link) from the webhook or auth flow, not from the browser.
- Happy path: sign up → pay in Stripe test mode → confirmation screen → email. Include a failed-payment state that does not grant access. Settings, teams, admin, and extra CRUD wait.
- Point Supabase Auth redirects and the Stripe webhook (`/api/stripe/webhook`) at the public preview origin, and update them when that URL changes.

## Secrets
Publishable and anon keys may ship to the frontend. The Stripe secret and the Supabase service role stay on the backend. Name every variable in `.env.example`. Never commit `.env`.

## Agents
Claude Code implements the app and wiring. GitHub hosts the repository. Supabase provides auth, Postgres, and storage. Stripe handles checkout. Resend sends the email.

## Done when
A reviewer can sign up, pay in Stripe test mode, land on a confirmation screen, and receive the email. A failed payment does not grant access.

starterPrompts.label: Subscription SaaS
starterPrompts.prompt: Ship a subscription SaaS MVP as a Vite React frontend plus a thin Express API. @supabase can handle auth and Postgres. @stripe can take Checkout for the plan. @resend can send the welcome email. @claude-code can implement it. @github can host the repository.

channels.name: Ship ecommerce
channels.description: Ship a small store: catalog, cart, Stripe checkout, and an order email.
channels.spec:
Goal: Ship a small store — 3–8 products, a cart, checkout, and one order email. Not a SaaS app and not a marketing page.

## Stack
Two processes, not a fullstack monolith. pnpm, ESM.

- **Frontend:** Vite + React + TypeScript. React Router. Tailwind is fine. Catalog, product page, cart, checkout success. Call the API with relative `/api` URLs. Port 5173.
- **Backend:** a thin Express (or Hono) TypeScript server. JSON REST. Port 3001. Stripe Checkout sessions, webhooks, Resend, and secret-bearing work live only here.
- **Do not** use Next.js, Remix, Nest, Shopify, Medusa, Saleor, or WooCommerce. No React Server Components, no server actions.
- Layout: `frontend/`, `backend/`, root `package.json` scripts, and `.env.example`.
- Vite `server.proxy`: `/api` → `http://127.0.0.1:3001` so the browser uses one origin.

## Store slice
Selling software access (SaaS, unlock, metered API) belongs in Ship paid MVP. A marketing-only page belongs in Ship landing page.

- **Catalog:** 3–8 products. Hardcoded JSON or a small Supabase `products` table. Variants optional. No inventory math, no discounts, no CMS or admin.
- **Cart:** client cart (localStorage is fine) plus a server checkout session built from those line items. Validate prices on the server — never trust the client amount. An empty cart has a clear state.
- **Checkout:** Stripe Checkout with line items, not subscriptions. Guest checkout is enough. Accounts are optional.
- **Fulfillment:** persist the order in Supabase on `checkout.session.completed`. Make that webhook idempotent. Resend sends the order confirmation. Digital goods: a download link in that email. Merch: collect a shipping address in Checkout and use a flat shipping rate. No live carrier rates, no tax APIs.
- Point the Stripe webhook (`/api/stripe/webhook`) at the public preview origin, and update it when that URL changes.

## Secrets
Publishable and anon keys may ship to the frontend. The Stripe secret and the Supabase service role stay on the backend. Name every variable in `.env.example`. Never commit `.env`.

## Agents
Claude Code implements the store and wiring. GitHub hosts the repository. Firecrawl scrapes a reference shop URL when the human provides one (messaging, branding, visuals); rebuild a distinct store, do not copy it. Supabase stores products (if not hardcoded) and orders. Stripe handles Checkout with line items. Resend sends the order email.

## Done when
A reviewer can add a product to the cart, pay in Stripe test mode, and receive the order email. A replayed webhook does not create a second order.

Vite React frontend plus a thin Express API. @stripe can take Checkout with line items. @supabase can store orders. @resend can send the receipt and download. @claude-code can implement it. @github can host the repository.
